[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Superultra's Favorite Permutation** [CF 2037C · Superultra's Favorite Permutation](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/2037/C){rating="1000"}

Partition by parity. Two numbers of the same parity have an even sum, and every even sum here is at least $1 + 3 = 4$, hence composite; so inside an all-even block and an all-odd block every neighbour pair is safe. Only the one **seam** between the blocks (even $+$ odd, an odd sum) can be prime. Make it a multiple of $3$: if the even block ends with $E$, start the odd block with the odd $o \in \{1, 3, 5\}$ that has $E + o \equiv 0 \pmod 3$; then $E + o \ge 9$ is composite. This needs $5 \le n$; for $n \le 4$ no answer exists.

[Solved in full in @sec-part-p4-b.]{.card-link}

:::
